The master-planned campus was the result of an endowment given by American industrialist James Buchanan Duke. Duke made his fortune in nearby Durham, North Carolina just several miles from the Duke Campus. The tobacco industry was booming in Durham in the early 1900’s. The architecture firm responsible for the Empire State Building consulted on the design of this bank in the 1930’s. The original bank vault is still downstairs. A federal antitrust broke up Duke’s American Tobacco Company in 1911. Prior, the company produced 80% of tobacco products in the United States.
